data.title: NetEase UU Remote to Launch VIP Service on December 1, Keeping Basic Remote Control Free
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, NetEase UU Remote plans to launch VIP and SVIP paid services on December 1, 2026, while keeping basic remote-control features free with no usage or time limits, queues, or ads. Recurring monthly subscriptions cost 24 yuan for VIP and 88 yuan for SVIP. Benefits include up to 4K resolution at 144 frames per second, multi-channel relay, multi-screen control, and priority customer service. Users who register before December 1 can claim a 50% discount on an annual card, equivalent to about 9.9 yuan per month.

data.title: Tech Leaders Don Leather Jackets for Jensen Huang; Kalanick Plans Nvidia HQ Protest
data.description: According to Jin10, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick wore a black leather jacket at an investor conference in Austin, Texas, alongside Antonio Gracias, a close friend of Elon Musk and a longtime investor who was also wearing one. Gracias said Kalanick’s jacket looked like Jensen Huang’s. Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder, was known for wearing a black leather jacket and was removed as the chipmaker’s CEO last week. “We need to get Huang back,” Kalanick said. Calls from Silicon Valley figures for Huang’s reinstatement continued on Wednesday, despite Nvidia’s board chair saying the company had no intention of bringing him back. Kalanick said he planned to show up at Nvidia’s offices with a “wafer-studded megaphone” and lead employees in a strike protest.

data.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames Itself Finney Foundation for Open Technology, Names First Fellows
data.description: The Bitcoin Policy Institute said it has changed its name to the Finney Foundation for Open Technology and announced its first group of fellows. According to Foresight News, the foundation said it will support open technologies, including open-source AI, digital cash, and encrypted communications, through research, policy recommendations, and educational programs. The fellows are Preston Byrne, Samo Burja, Christian Jauregui, Jonathan Looi, Jesse Posner, Freddie New, Noland Arbaugh, Chris Lengerich, Marko Jukic, and Knower. Their areas of focus include free speech; governance and emerging technologies; economics; national security; AI and democracy; space and industrial policy; Bitcoin and law; machine learning and health; and biotechnology.

data.title: A16z: Security and Delegation Challenges Slow Enterprise AI Agent Adoption
data.description: A16z says permissions and verifiability, rather than payments, are the biggest barriers to deploying AI agents in businesses. According to PANews, 69% of surveyed IT and security decision-makers said security concerns are slowing deployment, while only 27% believe existing identity systems can manage agents at scale; crypto teams could apply their experience with signing and delegated authorization to tasks held up by approval requirements.

data.title: Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Falls 2.1% to Its Lowest Close Since June
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Globe and Mail, Canada's S&P/TSX Composite fell 2.1% on November 18, dropping 737.25 points to 34,578.05, its largest one-day decline in nearly five months and lowest close since June 10. The index fell more than major U.S. benchmarks and closed at its lowest level since June. It has declined more than 6% from its August record high as metal and energy stocks sold off; companies in those sectors account for about one-third of the benchmark's weighting. The materials sector fell 5.4%, with Agnico Eagle Mines down 6.3%. Gold fell 3.4% to a 14-month low, while copper dropped 5.25%, its steepest percentage decline in 19 months. U.S. crude futures settled 3.2% lower at $83.26 a barrel. The energy and financial sectors fell 3.8% and 2.2%, respectively.

data.title: Calls for Jensen Huang’s Return Continue as Uber Co-Founder Threatens Nvidia Protest
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick said at an investors’ conference in Austin, Texas, that he would take a wafer-covered megaphone to Nvidia’s offices and lead employees in a strike to demand Jensen Huang’s return as CEO. Nvidia’s chairman has said the company has no intention of bringing Huang back, but calls for his reinstatement continued among Silicon Valley figures on Wednesday.

Kalanick compared the dispute to his own fight to remain Uber CEO; he resigned under pressure in 2017. At the DealBook conference on Wednesday, Elon Musk compared Huang’s removal to dropping Michael Jordan during a winning streak and reiterated that he would hire Huang. OpenAI President Greg Brockman called Huang “one of a kind,” while CEO Sam Altman said it was hard to imagine the AI industry without him. Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey said no one could replace Huang at this important moment.

On X, venture capitalist and SV Angels founder Ron Conway questioned whether Nvidia’s board had lost its objectivity, saying it had reached a conclusion about Huang before completing its own internal investigation. Pershing Square founder Bill Ackman also sharply criticized the directors, calling the board’s actions shocking given the company’s size and importance to the United States and the world.

In his first public remarks since leaving the CEO role on Tuesday, Huang said he would return if the board believed doing so was in the best interests of shareholders, employees, the company and the United States.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Singapore Issues S$100 Million in Tokenized Treasury Bills, Plans AI Agent Identity Protocol
data.description:
Singapore issued S$100 million in tokenized Singapore Treasury bills this month, settled using the Singapore-dollar central bank digital currency, and plans a unified identity-verification protocol for AI agents. According to Odaily, Monetary Authority of Singapore Managing Director Chia Der Jiun said AI agents could transfer funds and allocate assets faster, potentially creating liquidity and financial stability risks even when incentives are small. Financial institutions may need to limit transactions initiated by AI agents, while regulators assess their impact on financial stability.

Chia cautioned against giving personal AI agents financial account login credentials, saying their security cannot yet be adequately ensured. The planned “Know Your Agent” protocol would allow banks and payment providers to verify agents’ identities, permissions and authorization scopes. The authority will also test using AI agents to monitor liquidity positions and make payments through tokenized deposits or stablecoins.

The tokenized Treasury bills were settled with Singapore’s central bank digital currency and were worth approximately US$78 million. The authority plans to work with industry participants to bring more commonly used collateral, including foreign government securities and money market funds, onto digital platforms.

data.title: U.S. Crude, Gasoline and Distillate Stocks Remain Low as EIA Factor Amplifies Apparent Build
data.description: According to Jin10, combined U.S. crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories remain well below levels from the same period last year and the five-year average. Commercial crude inventories rose by about 3.4 million barrels this week, with the apparent build significantly affected by SPR releases and a sharp positive swing in the EIA adjustment factor.
